rationale: This is a pure deflator swap on the archive's leading IncrementalProfitConversion (at → wcap+dlc, since che cancels algebraically), and the stated rationale is internally shaky — dividing by a small, sometimes near-zero operating base amplifies rather than "compresses" heavy tails, so the claimed fmb fix is not what the expression naturally delivers.

This is the mechanical crossing of two already-evaluated archive signals (WeakestLinkIncrementalConversion's MIN rule and ThreeYearIncrementalConversion's horizon) with no new economic claim beyond "both worked separately," and it pays a real coverage cost (0.093) for an expected outcome that is a weighted average of the two parents.

Applying a severity statistic (TS_MAX) to the profit-benchmarked gap is a genuinely different temporal moment from the archive's streak-count and from WorstYearAccrualAggression's raw-accrual version, though the omission of WINSOR on a five-year maximum of an unbounded ratio is a construction weakness likely to inject outlier noise into the leg.

The MIN reduces algebraically to benchmarking the working-capital build against min(ΔGP, ΔNI), which is a coherent and economically defensible conservatism restriction on a single leg rather than a duplicate of the weakest-link architecture, but the two benchmarks are highly correlated so the incremental information over the existing gross-line signal is likely small.

The expression rewards firms whose cost of goods is growing fastest — Δcogs enters with a positive sign — which contradicts the earnings-quality story and inverts the logic of the archive's own AccrualBuildWithCostOverhang, and the economics substantially duplicate OverproductionVsCostBase.

Recasting the conversion gap in per-revenue intensity space is a substantively different normalization from the asset-deflated dollar difference and is internally consistent (both terms share units), but it is close to a raw-difference repackaging of two of the archive's weakest components (WorkingCapitalIntensityDrift and the margin-change leg), so the upside is modest.
